scope: read-only CI phase and current native test critical-path analysis; not a matched performance experiment

profile.attribution_limit: The profile combines loading, analysis and execution; it does not attribute the pre-first-TestRunner interval to a specific phase.

bridge_junit.note: JUnit case-time sums overlap across shards and are not wall time. TestRunner starts about 16s before the first pytest line in shard logs; no measured phase attribution is available.

conditional_12_app_labels.interpretation: This is interval removal from one observed invocation, not a speedup estimate or a matched selection experiment.

fixture_observation.scope: Session-scoped once per shard; the current four-shard target pays four starts, not one per test case.
fixture_observation.other_scopes: Kubernetes API server kubeconfig and DB templates are session scoped; Gateway, History, App, Sandbox, Runtime and per-test DB clone are function scoped for isolation. No evidence supports weakening these lifetimes.

independent_selected_run.use_limit: Different source, target set and cache state; descriptive contrast only, not a control.

proposed_falsifiable_probe.assertions_and_cases: All 24 cases retained identically; only shard count varies.
required_measurements: unique physical TestRunner execution IDs, stage/status/cache/link type
per-run TestRunner envelope and per-shard action interval/CPU/queue
JUnit case names/outcomes and cleanup failures
proposed_falsifiable_probe.decision_rule: Compare the max shard/target tail and worker/queue costs. Do not adopt a new shard count unless the physical ABBA evidence shows a useful tail improvement without increased failure/cleanup or resource contention.
proposed_falsifiable_probe.limits: This is a single-target distribution experiment, not a complete CI saving claim. Other retained tails in the 5699 run were approximately 84.6-90.7s.
